criteria: Actual clone, worktree add, branch switch, merge and manual-merge completion fixtures invoke integration and converge without a user executing apply; unsupported Git integration reports its coverage accurately.
Ensure combines authorization, registration and selected-scope reconciliation through the existing safety engine; unchanged runs preserve managed bytes/generation and perform no unrelated scans.
Untrusted roots, collisions, replaced parents, busy locks and pending recovery cannot be converted to success or silently repaired; hooks never claim to roll back completed Git actions.
Inactive-branch handling distinguishes verified branch absence from deleted, sparse, unreadable or conflicted input; interrupted readiness refuses completion after its control files change.
Owned hook installation/removal preserves unrelated hooks/settings, suppresses configured and directory hooks for MASK internal Git commands, and prevents recursion.
Native Claude and Codex startup/worktree scenarios record actual versions and first-prompt discovery or an explicit fallback limitation; a warning-only adapter is not called a strict gate.
Native Windows and macOS readiness/launcher paths receive focused direct checks; worktree removal and unavailable-root handling preserve ownership and are independently tested.
rfcs.title: Automatic workspace readiness for clone, worktree, branch and agent startup

criteria: Two private/public-style local bare remotes expose independent taps and nested/root packages; name ambiguity, path/ref ambiguity and conflicting aliases are actionable rather than silently selected.
Source identity checks bind the approved repository and transport policy, not just the basename; credential-bearing/unsupported URLs and unapproved redirects refuse without leaking secrets.
Copy import preserves byte provenance and notices, refuses existing unrelated destinations, records local adaptations, and performs no commit/push unless separately authorized.
Adversarial package fixtures cannot traverse paths, introduce special entries, run hooks/filters/package scripts, silently activate a plugin, or bypass bounded resource limits.
Source lifecycle and legacy-config migration preserve current ownership and old declarations; removing a referenced source refuses and reads/dry-runs remain observational.
Public CLI/capabilities describe resolution, catalog-only addition, mutation/network boundaries and provenance verification levels with deterministic errors.
rfcs.title: Multiple sources, taps, curated imports and upstream provenance

criteria: Two worktrees simultaneously use distinct immutable versions of one skill, and source authoring/ref movement changes neither deployment until an explicit selected update.
Locks reproduce raw package bytes across fixture machines; digest, package path, source identity, executable mode, malformed lock and moved-ref errors fail closed.
Ensure restores available exact artifacts, optionally hydrates only approved locked content, never resolves latest or rewrites lockfiles, and reports unavailable exact commits honestly.
Planner/executor/adoption/recovery correctly retarget an unchanged owned legacy or old-artifact link to a new artifact and preserve collisions, rather than retaining the old target.
Interruptions before/after lock, link and state effects preserve bounded v3 recovery; configuration/state migrations preserve exact legacy rollback bytes and reject concurrent edits.
Explicit migration covers project and personal consumers, dirty/unborn sources, old pending journals, schema-incompatible old programs, and direct-entrypoint escape paths.
Cache preparation, retention, dev-link exceptions and scoped publishing cannot silently alter other consumers, delete authoring history or claim atomicity across readers/devices.
rfcs.title: True version pinning, immutable deployment artifacts and recoverable migration

criteria: The same skill has independently configurable personal and project agent sets, with new selections defaulting to all supported/enabled agents and no executable-detection side effects.
V1 migration preserves explicit and inherited target behavior; per-skill edits/locks/plans remain guarded and no-op stable.
Generic, absent and agent/platform-specific metadata produce distinct truthful reports; explicit incompatibilities block, and conditional/inapplicable bindings are not called installed.
Multi-source name conflicts, conflicting profiles and user/project duplicate names are explained without overwriting content, silently renaming packages or assuming host precedence.
A single adapter contract drives paths/capabilities/validation, and existing native Claude/Codex scope tests cover the change; additional agents stay unadvertised until independently proven.
rfcs.title: Per-skill scope-specific agent targeting and advertised compatibility

criteria: Export/import round-trips selections and exact content locks between different machine/home/source paths without including credentials, registry identities, journals or launchers.
Incremental and replace modes preserve their declared ownership scopes; exported all-agent behavior and optional frozen-agent behavior are explicit and tested.
Bundle expansion/refresh is deterministic, source-revision bound and stale-plan guarded; overlapping bundles/manual selections do not cause accidental removals.
Profile subscription/removal preserves local contributions and reports version/target conflicts, unapproved sources, unavailable artifacts and offline freshness honestly.
One public import-and-apply path bootstraps selected personal scope through normal validation/recovery, with native Windows/macOS focused tests and no internal-state editing.
rfcs.title: Portable personal selections, reusable bundles and profile composition

criteria: Where-used accurately joins source-qualified skill identities to each project/personal consumer, agent, origin and artifact, without conflating duplicate names or inferring unknown host loading.

Update reports include supporting-file/binary/metadata/provenance changes and affected consumers even when membership is unchanged, while distinguishing unaffected pinned consumers from legacy shared-source impact.
Reports and application use the same frozen candidate/plan; source/ref/control-file movement stales a guarded plan, while formatting changes do not.
Inspection preserves state and unmanaged content, scopes filesystem/network work explicitly, and labels unavailable consumers and stale fleet receipts.
Compact text/JSON and optional offline HTML safely display untrusted skill content with escaping/redaction; focused query workloads record actual bounded work.
rfcs.title: Where-used inventory, update diffs and deployment impact reports

criteria: Enrollment binds stable device/controller identities, permitted scopes/sources and host transport identity, and rejects changed/revoked/unknown peers without changing user SSH security settings.
Bounded framed RPC accepts only the fixed action schema; malformed messages, shell metacharacters, wrong device IDs and arbitrary paths cannot invoke generic remote execution.
Each remote mutation uses the ordinary local planner/lock/journal; duplicate operation IDs, changed payloads, disconnects and timeouts produce queryable truthful outcomes.
Exact package transfer validates paths/digests and never forwards credentials or unrelated private content; unavailable authentication remains a prerequisite.
Native Windows/macOS transport and launcher checks record actual host/runtime results, while fixture-only tests remain labelled as such.
Controller/device signing and receipt validation use the established provider with separate namespaces and no unsigned silent fallback for unattended requests.
rfcs.title: Explicit fleet enrollment, device identity and bounded remote transport

criteria: A single name-or-GitHub-URL fleet install request composes copy/tap resolution, exact locking, authorized source/control publication, deployment and a per-device report without manual internal-state edits.
Frozen device/scope sets, local contribution preservation and source/package identity prevent unexpected project edits, hidden source enrollment or skill-name ambiguity.

Signed monotonic desired revisions and compare-and-swap publication handle two controllers, duplicate deliveries, replay, rollback-as-new-intent and revoked peers without silent last-writer overwrite.
Offline, unknown, incompatible, recovery-required, canceled and superseded devices are reported distinctly; incomplete rollouts never claim installed everywhere or reuse stale receipts.
An opt-in runner catches up to the latest approved state with bounded polling/backoff, preserves scheduler ownership, never upgrades upstream/programs implicitly, and resumes after interruptions.
Actual two-machine macOS/native-Windows rollout and offline catch-up evidence is recorded, or that acceptance stays open with the exact environmental limitation.
Failure between import/publication/remote apply/receipt steps is resumable and truthful, and reports preserve the difference between filesystem verification and host discovery.
rfcs.title: Declarative fleet rollouts, optional continuous convergence and completion reports

criteria: Optional facade installation does not alter core runtime requirements and advertises only implemented tools/protocol capabilities.
Tool operations produce the same selections/plans/effects/errors as the CLI and cannot bypass scope/source/device authorization, recovery or ownership checks.
Protocol negotiation, malformed inputs, output separation, bounded content and secret redaction pass direct client/fixture checks using the selected SDK.
Cancellation/disconnect/reconnect preserves durable operation truthfulness, and actual supported-client discovery/tool invocation is recorded before claiming host support.
rfcs.title: Optional MCP facade over the MASK management API

criteria: Credential handles remain separate from values, and existing Git/SSH providers keep working without migration or a mandatory shared vault.
An optional sealed provider uses a pinned established encryption/signature implementation and enforces explicit recipient/purpose grants without plaintext in portable data or tool responses.
Locked/unavailable providers, rotation, revoked/offline recipients and recovery-key loss produce accurate outcomes rather than silent fallback or premature completion.
Synthetic-secret leakage checks and actual selected native provider tests support the advertised exposure boundary; production credential changes are not part of fixture acceptance.
rfcs.title: Credential-provider references and an optional encrypted fleet vault

criteria: Threat/effect documentation distinguishes integrity, authorization, deployment, host loading and content safety, with explicit non-goals and no universal safety claim.
Core boundary tests and provider/dependency inventory are reused in a compact trust report that labels dirty/unsigned/unverified conditions truthfully.

A proposed public release has an explicitly authorized distribution/license decision, independently bootstrapped artifact verification and reproducible verification instructions; no publication is assumed.
Key rotation/revocation and update-channel rollback/freeze considerations are documented/tested at the selected provider boundary, without adding an unrequested automatic program updater.
rfcs.title: Public trust evidence and staged supply-chain hardening

criteria: Live import preserves historical RFCs/cards/counters, uses real reservations and baseline commits, and imports one closeout per RFC with no fabricated evidence.
Readiness, multi-source/pinning/targeting, composition/reporting and fleet milestones have focused integrated evidence and current public docs/capabilities that match what shipped.
Actual canonical AgentSkills management guidance and selected metadata/bundle/provenance handoffs are recorded by upstream revision and verified locally without duplicate tracker ownership.
Explicit selected-scope migrations preserve declarations, user data, ownership/recovery and source history on native macOS/Windows; unknown/unavailable acceptance stays open.

The real one-request fleet story demonstrates exact revisions, online/offline reporting and catch-up on distinct devices; optional MCP/vault/public-release work remains separately tracked and does not falsify core status.
rfcs.title: Staged migration, agent workflow handoff and personal-use acceptance
